section_summary.extract_value: This section reports bivariate correlations computed separately for women and men between body-related variables and MAIA subscales, noting mostly small-to-moderate positive correlations and some sex-specific patterns. Two statistically significant sex differences in correlation coefficients were identified (Self-Regulation with Body Appreciation, p = .029; Body Listening with Overweight Preoccupation, p = .026), and subsequent regression analyses used combined data controlling for sex.
section_summary.evidence_source: Bivariate correlations, conducted separately for women and men, between all variables are reported in Table 1. ... Despite the large number of comparisons, very few statistically significant differences were observed and only two statistically significant differences were identified within the relationships of interest: the correlation coefficients for Self-Regulation and Body Appreciation (p = .029) and between Body Listening and Overweight Preoccupation (p = .026). Therefore, rather than conducting regressions separately for each sex, we chose to conduct hierarchical multiple regression analyses utilising the data from both men and women, controlling for sex in the first step.
